वंश वंश, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. वन्,
to sound, or connected with rt. वङ्क्), a bamboo
cane, bamboo; a staff; a term for the rafters and laths
fastened to the beams of a house (as generally made
of split bamboos), or laths running across a roof [cf.
प्राचीन-वंश, प्राग्-वंश], a cross-beam, joint;
a sort of sugar-cane; the Śāl tree, Shorea Robusta;
a reed-pipe, tube, flute, pipe, fife; the back-bone,
spine [cf. पृष्ठ-व्˚]; the central projecting part
of a cimeter or sabre; the joints in a bamboo; the
line of a pedigree or genealogy (from its resemblance
to the succession of joints in a bamboo), a lineage,
race, family, stock; offspring, a son; a dynasty, race
of kings; a succession or collection of similar things
(as of chariots, stars, &c.), an assemblage, multitude,
host; a particular measure of length (= 10 Hastas);
bamboo-manna; N. of Viṣṇu ?; (आ), f., N. of an
Apsaras (a daughter of Prādhā); (ई), f. a flute,
pipe; an artery, vein; a particular weight (= 4 Kar-
shas); bamboo-manna; [cf. Goth. rausa, ‘a reed;’
Old Germ. rohr.]

वन् 1. वन्, cl. 1. P. वनति, &c., to
sound; to serve, honour, worship, help,
aid; cl. 8. P. A. वनोति, वनुते, ववान, ववने,
&c. (Vedic forms वनाति, वनास्, ववन्म, वव्ने,
वंसाम, वंसीमहि, वनुयाम, वनवत् [ =
वनुयात् = हिंस्यात्], वनिषत्, वनुषन्त, वनि-
षन्त, वन्त [as if cl. 2], वंस्व, वावनस्, वा-
वन्धि), Inf. वनितुम् (Ved. [प्र]वन्तवे), to
ask, request, beg, seek; (the following senses are
mostly peculiar to Ved.), to like, love; to wish, de-
sire; to obtain, acquire, procure, furnish, offer, give;
to gain or obtain by conquest, become master of,
conquer, possess; to make ready, prepare for, aim
at; to hurt, injure: Caus. वनयति (when com-
bined with preps.), वानयति, -यितुम्, to cause to
sound, &c.; to act, transact business; to hurt, kill;
(the rt. वन् in cl. 10. 1. वानयति, वनति, &c.
also means ‘to confide,’ ‘believe in,’ but in this sense
is a various reading for rt. 2. तन्, q. v.); [cf. per-
haps Gr. ὀνίνημι, ὀνήσω, ὄνειαρ; Lat. Ven-us, ve-
nustas, veneror; Goth. vens; Old Germ. wini,
winia, wunna; Angl. Sax. wyn, ge-wenian, to-
wenan; (according to some also) Gr. φένω, φόνος,
φονεύς; Lat. funus; Hib. bana, ‘death.’]

2. वन् (only used in the loc. and gen. pl. वंसु,
वनाम्), Ved. = 1. वन, a wooden vessel, (accord-
ing to Sāy. वंसु = उदकेषु); = अरणि, the wood
used for kindling fire by attrition, (according to Sāy.
गर्भो वनाम् = the offspring of the pieces of wood
so used); love, worship (according to some).

1. वन, अम्, n. (for 2. वन see p. 885, col. 1), a
wood, forest, grove, thicket, a quantity of lotuses or
other plants growing in a thick bed or cluster (e. g.

timber; a wooden vessel or barrel (for the Soma
juice); ‘the vessel in the sky,’ i. e. a cloud (Ved.);
water (Ved.); a fountain, spring; a place of abode,
residence; dwelling in a forest, residence abroad;
(according to Naigh. I. 4) = रश्मि, a ray of light;
(according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda I. 24, 7) light (=
तेजस्); the body of a carriage (so suggested by
modern scholars as an interpretation in Ṛg-veda VIII.
34, 18); worshipping; (perhaps) longing, earnest
desire; Cyperus Rotundus; (आ), f. = अरणि, wood
used to produce fire by attrition; (in Ṛg-veda III.
1, 13) Wood for so kindling fire personified; (ई), f.
a wood, forest; (अस्), m., N. of a son of Uśīnara;
of one of the ten orders of mendicants founded by

female of an animal; a particular metre, four times

ban, ‘a woman.’]
—वनिता-द्विष्, ट्, m. hating

woman like a serpent, serpent of a woman.
—व-
निता-मुख, आस्, m. pl. ‘woman-faced,’ N. of a
people.
—वनिता-विलास, अस्, m. the wantonness of
women.
वनितास, अम्, n., N. of a family.

वनितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, an asker, &c.; one who
possesses or owns, a possessor (Ved.).

वनिन्, ई, इनी, इ (fr. the rt. and in some meanings
fr. 1. वन), Ved. worshipping, honouring, serving;
desiring, wishing for; distributing, bestowing, giving
(said of the Maruts &c.); rain-dispensing; having
water, granting water, abounding in water; belong-
ing to a wood, living in a wood; filled with or
possessed of wood; (ई), m. a tree; the Soma plant;
a Brāhman residing in the forest, one in the third
stage of life, a Vānaprastha.

वनिन, अम्, n., Ved. anything growing in a
forest, a tree.
वनिल, see Gaṇa Kāśādi to Pāṇ. IV. 2, 80.

वनिष्ठु, उस्, m., Ved. part of the entrails of
[]
an animal offered in sacrifice; the rectum; (according
to others) a part of the intestines near the omentum,
(Sāy. = स्थविरान्त्र.)
वनिष्णु, incorrect for वनिष्ठु.

वनीय, Nom. P. वनीयति, &c., to beg, ask
alms; to entreat, request.
वानीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be woven, &c.

वनीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, asking or obtaining more,
obtaining most; to be honoured, to be favoured,
(Sāy. = सम्भजनीय = सम्भाव्य); imparting
or bestowing most.

वनीवन्, आ, आ, अ (an Intensive form), asking for,
demanding, (Sāy. = वनन-वत्.)

वनु, उस्, m., Ved. one who plots against or
injures, a malignant or malicious person, (Sāy. =
हिंसक); an adherent (?).

वनुष (fr. वनुस्), Nom. A. वनुषते, &c.,
Ved. to obtain, acquire; (Sāy.) to worship.

वनुष्य (fr. वनुस्), Nom. P. A. वनुष्यति,
-ते, &c., Ved. to have a design upon, plot against,
seek to injure, to be fond of battle; to emulate
(with inst.); to overpower, defeat, attack, (according
to Naigh. II. 12 = क्रुध्यति; according to Nirukta
V. 2 = हन्ति); (A.) to wish for, desire, (Sāy. on Ṛg-
veda IX. 7, 6. वनुष्यते = सेव्यते.)

वनुष्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, seeking to injure, ma-
levolent, hostile, an enemy.

वनुस्, उस्, उस्, उस्, Ved. desiring, anxious for, eager,
zealous; devoted, attached to, loving; enjoying, an
enjoyer, worshipping, a worshipper, honourer, (Sāy.
= सम्भक्तृ); (उस्), m. any one eager to injure
(others), an enemy, plotter, warrior; the act of possess-
ing, enjoying, distributing, (Sāy. = सम्भजन.)
वनेज्य, अस्, m. a kind of mango.
वनेयु, उस्, m., N. of a son of Raudrāśva.
वन्ति, इस्, f., see Pāṇ. VI. 4, 39.

वान्ति, इस्, f. the act of vomiting, ejecting from
the mouth.
—वान्ति-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, causing vomiting,
emetic; (त्), m. the thorny plant Vangueria Spinosa.
—वान्ति-द, अस्, आ, अम्, causing vomiting, emetic;
(आ), f. a medicinal plant (= कटुकी); Helleborus
Niger or Wrightea Antidysenterica or Calotropis
Gigantea.

वन्तृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who enjoys or possesses,
a possessor, owner, (Sāy. = सम्भक्तृ.)

वन्य, अस्, आ, अम्, growing in woods, of or be-
longing to a wood, forest, produced in a wood, living
in woods, wild, savage; being or existing in a wood
(said of Agni, Ved.); made of wood, wooden; (अस्),
m. an animal of the forest, wild animal, wild beast;
a wild plant; N. of particular wild plants (= वन-
शूरण, वाराही-कन्द, देव-नाल); (आ), f. a
multitude of groves, a large forest; abundance of
water, a flood, deluge; N. of various plants, Physalis
Flexuosa; = मद्गु-पर्णी, गोपाल-कर्कटी, गुञ्जा,
मिश्रेया, भद्र-मुस्ता, गन्ध-पत्त्रा; (अम्),
n. anything grown in a wood, the fruit or roots of
wild plants; = त्वच; [cf. other meanings of the
word वन्य in चक्षुर्-व्˚, अजीत-पुनर्वण्य.]
—वन्य-द्विप, अस्, m. a wild elephant.
—वन्य-
पक्षिन्, ई, m. a wild bird, forest bird; [cf. पुर-
पक्षिन्.]
—वन्य-वृत्ति, इस्, f. forest fare.
—व-
न्याशन (˚य-अश्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, eating wild fruits, &c.
—वन्येतर (˚य-इत्˚), अस्, आ, अत्, different from
wild tame, civilized.

वान्या, f. a collection of woods, multitude of
groves or thickets; [cf. वन्या.]
वन्योपादकी, f. a kind of creeper.
वनर वनर, अस्, m. = वानर.

वानर, अस्, m. (fr. वनर, which is probably fr.
1. वन, ‘a wood;’ according to others fr. वा, ‘like,’
नर, ‘a man’), a monkey, ape; (ई), f. a female
monkey or ape; cowach, Carpopogon Pruriens; (अस्,
ई, अम्), belonging to a monkey, monkey-like.
—वा-
नर-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear to monkeys,’ the tree
Mimusops Kauki.
—वानराक्ष (˚र-अक्˚), अस्, m.
‘monkey-eyed,’ a wild goat.
—वानराघात (˚र-
आघ्˚), अस्, m. ‘monkey-stroke,’ i. e. ‘struck or in-
jured by monkeys,’ the tree Symplocos Racemosa
(commonly called Lodhra or Lodh).
—वानराप-
सद (˚र-अप्˚), अस्, m. a contemptible monkey.
—वानरेन्द्र (˚र-इन्˚), अस्, m. ‘monkey-chief,’
epithet of Sugrīva; of Hanu-mat.
—वानरेश्वर-
तीर्थ, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
वनर्गु वनर्-गु. See under वनस्, p. 884.
वनहबन्दि वनहबन्दि, N. of a place.
वनाहिर वनाहिर, अस्, m. a hog, wild boar.

वनीवाहन वनीवाहन, अम्, n. (an anoma-
lous Intens. fr. rt. 1. वह्), Ved. the act of carrying
or moving hither and thither.

वनौकस् वनौकस्, वनौषधि. See
p. 884, cols. 2, 3.
वन्तव वन्तव (?) , अस्, m. a proper N.

वन्द् वन्द् (connected with rt. वद्), cl.
1. A. (Ved. and ep. sometimes P.) वन्-
दते, ववन्दे (Ved. ववन्द, ववन्दिम), अवन्-
दिष्ट, वन्दितुम् (Ved. Inf. वन्दध्यै), to
praise, celebrate, laud, extol, eulogize, bless, pro-
nounce a blessing; to show honour, do homage,
salute respectfully, greet, make obeisance to; to
venerate, worship, adore: Pass. वन्द्यते, Aor.
अवन्दि, to be praised, &c.: Caus. वन्दयति, -यते,
-यितुम्, Aor. अववन्दत्, अववन्दत, to show
honour to any one, make obeisance to, greet respect-
fully.

वन्द, अस्, आ, अम्, praising, extolling; [cf. देव-
वन्द.]

वन्दा, f. a parasitical plant, the parasitical plant
Epidendrum Tesselatum, &c.; a female beggar or
mendicant; = वन्दि, वन्दी.

वन्दक, अस्, आ, m. f. a praiser, &c.; a parasitical
plant.
वन्दाक, अस्, m., आ, ई, f. a parasitical plant.

वन्दथ, अस्, m. a praiser, panegyrist, eulogist,
bard; one deserving praise.

वन्दद्-वार, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. blessing the mul-
titude, i. e. men, (in Sāma-veda I. 1, 2, 3, 6. for
वन्दे दारुम्, which is the correct reading in the
corresponding passage of the Ṛg-veda.)

वन्दद्-वीर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. blessing heroes,
(in Sāma-veda I. 4, 2, 3, 1. for मन्दद्-वीर,
which is the correct reading in the corresponding
passage of the Ṛg-veda.)

वन्दन, अस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi (described in
Ṛg-veda I. 112, 5. as having been cast into a well,
along with Rebha, by the Asuras, and rescued by the
Aśvins); (आ), f. praise, praising, worship, adoration;
a mark or sign worn on the body (made with ashes
&c.); (ई), f. making obeisance, reverence, worship,
adoring; begging, soliciting, asking; the hip (?) ; a
drug for reviving the dead; (अम्), n. the act of
praising, praise; obeisance to a Brāhman or superior
(by touching the feet &c.), reverence, adoration;
the face, mouth (= वदन); a parasitical plant
(perhaps a kind of lichen); a disease attacking the
limbs or joints, a cutaneous eruption, scrofula (some-
times personified as a demon).
—वन्दन-माला or
वन्दन-मालिका, f. a festoon suspended across gate-
ways (in honour of the arrival of any distinguished
personage, or on the occasion of a marriage or other
festival).
—वन्दन-श्रुत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved. listening to
praise, a hearer of praises, (Sāy. = स्तुतीनां श्रोतृ.)

वान्दन वान्दन, अस्, m. a patronymic of
Duvasyu (author of the hymn Ṛg-veda X. 100).

वन्दनीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised or wor-
shipped, praiseworthy, adorable, to be greeted with
homage, to be saluted or made obeisance to; (अस्),
m. a yellow-flowering Verbesina; (आ), f. the yellow
pigment called गो-रोचना, q. v.

वन्दमान, अस्, आ, अम्, praising, celebrating, pro-
nouncing a blessing, honouring, reverencing.

वन्दयित्वा, ind. (fr. the Caus.), having praised,
having saluted or shown honour to, having made
obeisance to.
वन्दार, अस्, m. a parasitical plant.

वन्दारु, उस्, उस्, उ, praising, celebrating; respect-
ful, reverential, civil, complimentary, polite; (उस्), m.
a panegyrist, bard; a proper N.; (उ), n. praise.

1. वन्दि, इस्, m. (for 2. वन्दि see col. 3), a praiser,
panegyrist, &c. (= वन्दिन्).

perly written बन्दि, बन्दी; probably connected
with rt. बन्ध्, cf. the Persian بنده for 1. वन्दि
see col. 2), a captive or prisoner in general
(male or female); a woman in captivity, female

—वन्दि-
ग्राह, अस्, m. ‘plunder-seizer,’ a housebreaker
(especially one breaking into a temple or place where
sacred fire is preserved).
—वन्दि-चौर, अस्, m. =
वन्दि-ग्राह above.
—वन्दी-कार, अस्, m. one who
commits robbery, a robber, thief, housebreaker, bur-
glar.
—वन्दी-कृ, cl. 8. P. A. -करोति, -कुरुते,
-कर्तुम्, to make captive, take prisoner, capture,
rob.
—वन्दी-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्, made prisoner, taken
captive.
—वन्दी-पाल, अस्, m. a keeper of prisoners,
a jailor.
वन्दित, अस्, आ, अम्, praised, extolled, celebrated.

वन्दितव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised or cele-
brated, laudable, to be treated with awe or respect,
one to whom obeisance is to be made.

वन्दितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, Ved. one who praises or
celebrates, a praiser.

वन्दिन्, ई, m. one who praises or extols, a praiser,
panegyrist, encomiast, bard, poet, herald (whose duty
is to proclaim the titles of a great man as he passes
along, or who sings the praises of a prince in
his presence or accompanies an army to chaunt
martial songs; these bards are regarded as belonging
to a distinct tribe, being considered the descendants
of a Kṣatriya by a Śūdra female); a captive, slave,
(in this sense more properly written बन्दिन्, cf.

2. वन्दि.)
—वन्दि-पाठ, अस्, m. the panegyric
of a bard or Vandin, eulogium.
वन्दिनीका or वन्दिनीया, f., N. of Dākṣāyaṇī.

वन्द्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be praised, laudable, com-
mendable, praiseworthy; to be reverentially saluted,
to be honoured or worshipped, adorable, very vene-
rable; to be regarded or respected; (अस्), m. a
proper N.; (आ), f. = वन्दा, a parasitical plant; =
गो-रोचना; N. of a Yakṣī.
—वन्द्य-ता, f. lauda-
bility, praiseworthiness, venerableness.

वन्द्यमान, अस्, आ, अम्, being praised or cele-
brated, being saluted or greeted.

वन्द्र, अस्, आ, अम्, praising, worshipping, honour-
ing, doing homage; (अस्), m. a worshipper, votary,
follower; (अम्), n. prosperity.

वन्दीक वन्दीक, अस्, m. (also written बन्-
दीक), N. of Indra.

वन्धा वन्धा, ind., see Gaṇa Ūry-ādi to
Pāṇ. I. 4, 61.
वन्धुर् वन्धुर्. See below.

वन्धुर्, m., Ved. = वन्धुर above; (in Atharva-
veda III. 9, 3. the sense is doubtful.)

वन्धुर वन्धुर, अम्, n. (probably con-
nected with rt. बन्ध् and perhaps more properly
written बन्धुर), the seat of a charioteer, the
fore part of a chariot or place at the end of the
shafts, a carriage-seat or driver's box; the frame-
work [cf. हिरण्य-व्˚] of a carriage, (the word वन्-
धुरम् occurs frequently in Ved. and is variously
explained by Sāy. as नीड-बन्धनाधार-भूतम्,
उन्नतानत-रूप-बन्धन-काष्ठम्, वेष्टि-
तं सारथेः स्थानम्, सारथ्य्-आश्रय-स्थानम्,
&c.; the car of the Aśvins, which is described as
‘three-wheeled’ as well as triple in other parts of
its construction, is said to be also त्रि-वन्धुर or
त्रि-बन्धुर, i. e. ‘having three poles or pieces
of wood for securing the occupant’ or ‘having a
triple standing-place or seat for the charioteer.’)
—वन्धुरे-ष्ठा, आस्, आस्, अम् (i. e. वन्धुरे,
loc. c. + स्था), Ved. standing or sitting on the
chariot-seat.

वन्धुरायु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. having a standing-
place in front or a seat for driving (said of the car
of the Aśvins).

वन्धुल वन्धुल, अस्, m. (also written बन्-
धुल, q. v.), N. of a Ṛṣi.

वन्र वन्र, अस्, m. (according to Uṇādi-s.
II. 28. fr. rt. 1. वन्), a co-partner, co-heir.
वान्त, वान्ति. See s. v.

वान्त वान्त, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. rt. वम्), vomited,
ejected from the mouth, effused; one who has vo-
mited; वान्ते, ind. when one has vomited; (अस्), m.,
N. of a Particular family of priests.
—वान्त-वृष्टि,
इस्, इस्, इ, (a cloud &c.) that has vomited out rain.
—वान्ताद (˚त-अद˚), अस्, m. ‘eating what is vomited,’
a dog.
—वान्ताशिन् (˚त-अश्˚), ई, m. ‘eating what is
vomited,’ a foul-feeding demon.

Brāhman of the third order who has passed through
the stages of student and householder and has left
his house and family for the woods, (see आश्रम);
a hermit, anchorite; a class of supernatural beings;
the tree Bassia Latifolia; the Palāśa tree, Butea
Frondosa.
—वानप्रस्थ-धर्म, अस्, m. the law
or duty of a Vānaprastha.
—वानप्रस्थाश्रम
(˚थ-आश्˚), अस्, अम्, m. n. the Āśrama or order of
a Vānaprastha.

वानल, अस्, m. (probably fr. 1. वन), the black
species of Tulasī or holy basil, Ocymum Sanctum.

वानस्पत्य, अस्, m. (fr. वनस्-पति), a tree the
fruit of which is produced from blossom (= पुष्प-
जात-फल-वृक्ष; cf. वनस्-पति, which is said

patya are the Mango, Eugenia, &c.).

—वा-
नीर-गृह, अम्, n. or आस्, m. pl. an arbour of reeds.
—वानीर-ज, अम्, n. a plant (= कुष्ठ, q. v.).
वानीर वानीर. See above.

वानीरक, अस्, m. a sort of rush or grass, Saccha-
rum Munja; [cf. मुञ्ज.]

वानेय, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to a wood
or to water, &c.; (अस्), m. the fragrant grass Cyperus
Rotundus.
वान्त्वा, ind. having vomited, &c.
